Why not put this as a priority to test out, in parallel with DankShading implementation? To be entirely fair I do wonder occasionally if the last 4s of the slot could be reduced to 2s. Although I haven't done a full analysis, the last couple of seconds prior to the next slot do appear to be significantly quieter in terms of CPU usage. (And yes I know that CPU usage hasn't been the main concern as far as the execution side is concerned, and that it would create a(nother) significant increase in bandwidth, and and and, just a thought that crosses my mind now and again.) <dankrad> Right, but if we were comfortable with higher throughput, it would make more sense to just increase the gas limit. Reducing to 10s slot would be useful in terms of reducing latency of transactions being included Higher gas limit makes things more bursty, though, compared to a reduced slot time. are you checking CPU usage of the beacon node or of the combo CL+EL... quieter time for one may not be for the other that's already building a block. In a world where we outsource all block production it may make sense, but then we probably switch to two shorter slots PBS This is the combo (both running on the same server). Attestations still seem to be the biggest amount of work on the consensus side, so depending on how PBS works it may be hard to significantly reduce the slot time whilst retaining the same level of security. Oh It will surely be larger, not reduced so 2 shorter slots, but each one longer than 6 seconds <dankrad> > <dankrad> gas limit is mainly to limit storage rather than computation though (re @allcoredevs_bot: <jgm> [reply]: Higher gas limit makes things more bursty, though, compared to a reduced slot time.) I think higher gas limit makes more sense rather than decreasing slot time I think it would also be easier to implement Also as said before beacon chain has more load on attestations than anything else. I would also assume that changing slot time would require an hard fork While gas limit does not Adrian Sutton 5243 you need to add a I opened two PRs to propose an epoch/slot/timestamp combo for Sepolia based on today's ACDC call, and the follow up conversation in <#892088344438255616> EL specs: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/716 Sepolia testnet page (best we have for CL, I think?): https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/30 If there are no objections in the next day or so, probably makes sense to merge them tomorrow so teams can start putting out releases early next week 🙂 Also, if an EL dev wants to share the expected fork ID, I can add that to the PR too 🙂

excerpts.author: 0x1984
excerpts.content: If block time can be reduced to 10 seconds from 13 seconds, it's already an impressive 25% improvement of ETH capacity - And can have more ETH burnt. Why not put this as a priority to test out, in parallel with DankShading implementation?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
To be entirely fair I do wonder occasionally if the last 4s of the slot could be reduced to 2s.  Although I haven't done a full analysis, the last couple of seconds prior to the next slot do appear to be significantly quieter in terms of CPU usage.

(And yes I know that CPU usage hasn't been the main concern as far as the execution side is concerned, and that it would create a(nother) significant increase in bandwidth, and and and, just a thought that crosses my mind now and again.)
